testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: Can you explain the difference between reference-based and reference-free evaluation in your own words?
testCases.actualOutput:
Certainly! The difference between reference-based and reference-free evaluation primarily revolves around the presence or absence of a predefined correct answer.

In reference-based evaluation, you have a specific answer key or a "golden dataset" that outlines what the correct answers should be for each test case. This means that when you evaluate the output of a model or system, you compare its results directly against this established reference. For example, if you were assessing a chatbot's responses, you would check how closely those responses match the expected answers that you already have documented.

On the other hand, reference-free evaluation occurs when there is no predefined answer key available. In this case, you don't have a specific correct answer to compare against. Instead, you might use a rubric or set of criteria to assess the quality of the output based on subjective measures or other qualitative factors. This type of evaluation is useful when you're exploring new areas or when the correct answers are not well-defined.

To summarize, if you can check the output against a known correct answer, it's reference-based; if you can't, it's reference-free. This distinction helps you determine how to approach the evaluation process depending on the resources and information available.
